extracted.intended_audience: senior news publishers and media executives (WAN-IFRA members, C‑Suite, commercial directors, executive editors)
extracted.subtask_description: A global industry benchmarking report summarising publishers' outlooks, strategic priorities and operational pressures to help news organisations compare strategy, performance and journalism with peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business outlook / company prospects
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether respondents convey a positive or negative outlook about their companies’ business prospects for the foreseeable future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes that 'more than half of the respondents conveying a positive outlook' in 2023-24; this is presented as a high‑level benchmark of publisher sentiment despite external challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers' approach to generating income across streams (subscriptions, advertising, other monetisation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report highlights that news publishers are 'looking closely at their revenue strategy' as a primary response to market pressures; use this to compare strategic emphasis on different revenue levers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Where publishers choose to allocate capital and resources (technology, talent, production, distribution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a key area publishers are reassessing — the report 'delves into these themes extensively' so track shifts in investment focus year‑on‑year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Areas of focus (editorial & commercial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific domains, products or initiatives publishers prioritise operationally or editorially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned alongside investment priorities as items publishers review; can include audience engagement, product development, vertical coverage, or commercial experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost management / operational efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers’ strategies to manage costs in response to rising expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context given: 'elevated inflation and interest rates, surging paper and printing expenses' — measure approaches to cost control, restructuring, and efficiency programmes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stance on AI and other technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisational position toward generative AI and other emerging technologies (adoption, restraint, policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report flags the 'surge of Generative AI' as a strategic challenge; publishers' stances (embrace, cautious, prohibitive) are presented as a material area for benchmarking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationships with platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: How publishers manage and negotiate changing relationships with major platforms (distribution, monetisation, data access).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called out as an ongoing strategic challenge — evaluate partnership policies, platform dependence, and diversification strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press freedom and freedom of expression challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which threats or constraints to press freedom and free expression impact editorial operations and strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among 'wider strategic challenges' that 'continue to vex many journalists and publishers' — assess legal, political and safety concerns affecting newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising market shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in advertising demand, formats and revenue that affect publisher commercial performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as a specific headwind ('continual shifts within advertising markets') — track ad revenue trends, format migration, and advertiser behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience behaviour changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Shifts in how audiences consume news (platforms, formats, paying behaviour) and their implications for product and strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited alongside advertising shifts as a key pressure; use to benchmark product decisions, engagement metrics and subscription strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational / macroeconomic pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: External financial pressures such as elevated inflation, higher interest rates, and rising supply costs (e.g., paper and printing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These contextual pressures are the drivers behind strategic change and should be included when comparing operational resilience and fiscal planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geopolitical risk exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact of geopolitical uncertainty (conflicts in Ukraine, the Middle East, etc.) on operations, markets and editorial risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report cites geopolitical uncertainty as a factor affecting publishers globally; use this to assess market-specific risk and contingency planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer benchmarking (strategy, performance, journalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the report to see how an individual publisher's strategies, performance and journalism 'ranks among their peers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report is presented as 'a good benchmark' — this is the overarching evaluative purpose: compare comparable metrics and qualitative practices against peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey methodology & sample transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Details about the survey basis: online survey to WAN‑IFRA members and senior media executives, conducted July–September 2023, available in four languages; 175 complete responses from 60 nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report provides respondent breakdowns (seniority: ~66% C‑Suite; roles: commercial directors/heads of strategy, executive editors; 58% from developed economies, 42% from developing). These methodological details are essential for judging representativeness and interpreting findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent seniority and role composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The organisational level and roles of survey participants (C‑Suite, commercial leads, executive editors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report specifies that a third (66%) are C‑Suite and another third are commercial leaders or executive editors — use this to weigh perspectives (business vs editorial) in the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and economic representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity of countries represented and distribution across developed vs developing economies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly notes 60 nations represented and World Bank classification split (58% developed / 42% developing) with examples of markets; important for assessing global applicability of insights.
